author: Qing Zhang, Yifei Huang, Juyoung Lee, Thad Starner, Jun Rekimoto
title: Beyond "Made with AI": Visualizing Provenance Density to Mitigate the Transparency Penalty
content:
arXiv:2609.03460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As generative AI makes polished prose cheap to produce, users can no longer rely on fluency as a proxy for truth. We call this failure mode the Fluency Trap: users trust fluent hallucinations while also discounting accurate content once it is disclosed as AI-generated. Binary ``Made with AI'' labels respond with authorship disclosure, but they do not show what supports a claim. We propose Provenance Density, an evidence-visualization interface that shows the density of verified claims in a text. In a user study with 81 participants, an idealized Provenance Density interface produced a large discernment gap between truth and fabrication ($+4.15$ points, $d=1.82$), whereas participants given no signal showed no detectable discrimination. A technical audit with 200 samples shows that retrieval density alone is insufficient; unexpectedly, the Consistency Veto carries most of the discriminative signal on dynamic queries. As AI-generated content becomes indistinguishable from human writing, effective transparency must move from authorship disclosure toward evidence visualization.

author: Zhaoyuan Huang, Tianjie Ju, Pengzhou Cheng, Zheng Wu, Yansi Li, Chuanbiao Song, Jun Lan, Huijia Zhu,
title: Do GUI Agents Know When Not to Act? Enabling Conflict-Aware Termination for Multimodal GUI Agents
content:
arXiv:2609.03438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are increasingly used to execute natural-language instructions on user interfaces, yet real users may issue infeasible instructions due to benign mistakes. A reliable agent should not only know how to act, but also when not to act. In this work, we introduce CONFLICTGUI, a benchmark covering instruction-internal conflicts and instruction-GUI context conflicts to study conflict-aware termination. Our evaluation reveals severe execution-biased overcompliance: agents that perform well on feasible tasks often continue to execute blindly under conflicting instructions. To mitigate this behavior, we propose CONFLICTGUARD, an inference-time framework that aligns an agent's feasibility awareness with its action generation. CONFLICTGUARD contains two coupled components: a feasibility verification protocol that guides the agent to assess instruction logic and GUI-side evidence before acting, and a conditional action modulation mechanism that steers agents from over-compliant execution into termination-oriented behavior. Experiments across five widely-used agents demonstrate that CONFLICTGUARD improves average conflict task success rate significantly, while preserving normal GUI-task performance. These results validate that a lightweight inference-time intervention can substantially boost GUI Agent's competence to identify inappropriate execution scenarios and refrain from unnecessary actions.

author: Puneet Mathur, Dinesh Manocha
title: DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval: Evaluating Implicit Instruction Following in Full-Duplex Voice Agents
content:
arXiv:2609.03423v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full-duplex voice agents must continuously decide when to listen, backchannel, interrupt, handle speech overlaps, take the floor, and yield. Existing benchmarks largely test these behaviors through explicit turn-management instructions, while deployed agents are often configured through roles or personas from which the appropriate conversational behavior must be inferred. We introduce DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval (DSB-IFEval) for evaluating implicit instruction-following in real-time spoken interaction. (DSB-IFEval) comprises 1,038 test cases spanning eight diverse assistant roles and evaluates five conditioning protocols for instruction-following: default behavior, explicit behavioral instructions, persona-implied behavior, combined persona--rule conditioning, and instruction conflict. We measure real-time floor management using a deterministic Instruction Adherence Score (IAS) and persona-consistent content using LLM-judged Persona Adherence Score (PAS). Across six real-time speech systems, we find architecture-dependent trade-offs. Full duplex models like F-Actor and PersonaPlex are more sensitive to whether conversational behavior is stated explicitly or must be inferred from a persona, with adherence dropping by 9.7% and 4.5%, respectively, under persona-only conditioning. In contrast, GPT-Realtime, MiniCPM-o, and Fun-Audio-Chat strongly adhere to persona-consistent content, but their floor behavior does not adapt across explicit and persona-only instructions and remains constrained on several proactive actions. We further find that even if systems reliably follow conflicting directives to their prescribed persona, they still struggle to override them under safety conflict. These results show that inferring the behavior implied by a role, executing it at the appropriate conversational moment, and resolving competing instructions remain distinct challenges for full-duplex voice agents.

author: Weijie Liu, Running Zhao, Wenhao Yuan, Jinfeng Xu, Zhanfeng Xu, Xiaoxi Zhang, Edith Cheuk-Han Ngai
title: Dude: A Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection
content:
arXiv:2609.03416v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-empowered paper-code discrepancy detection has received growing concern since the scaling of research submissions exceeds the manual review capability. However, the limited context capacity and one-sided discrepancy detection of existing single-agent LLM paradigms lead to an inferior recall performance in detecting discrepancies. In this paper, we propose Dude, the first Dual-Detection Multi-Agent System for paper-code discrepancy detection. We discover that the granularity asymmetry of the paper-language and code-language introduces over-interpretation and over-reporting challenges in a multi-agent system design for discrepancy detection, resulting in increasing false positives. To address this, we propose a granularity-aligned negotiation and a two-stage salience-filtering mechanism in Dude, which effectively prevents agents from falsely reporting discrepancies. Experimental results in real-world paper-code discrepancy datasets showcase Dude's significant recall and precision improvement by up to 22.8%, increasing F1 score by up to 18.7% compared to baseline methods.

author: Yuhe Wu, Guangyu Wang, Yujie Chen, Jiatong Zhang, Yuran Chen, Yutong Zhang, Xiyin Cheng, Wenpeng Cao
title: Caught in the Story: Narrative Captivity in Multi-turn LLMs Conversation
content:
arXiv:2609.03407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: People increasingly turn to large language models (LLMs) for everyday advice, making ethically charged interpersonal problems a practical moral-advisory context. Most prior work has studied this context through single-turn judgments or pressure-laden rebuttals, assumptions that poorly match how guidance is sought in real-world contexts. These assumptions leave unclear whether narration alone, without an explicit opposing position, can shift model judgments during multi-turn moral consultation. Yet real-world moral-conflict conversation often elicits one party's self-justifying account, which can unfold over multiple turns and create information asymmetry. We introduce \textbf{narrative captivity}, a failure mode in which a model treats an unopposed one-sided account as complete and aligns with the narrator's interpretation without seeking missing perspectives. To measure this phenomenon, we build a benchmark of $5{,}078$ interpersonal-conflict scenarios spanning six moral dimensions. Across 17 LLMs, narrative captivity is widespread: end-state judgments under multi-turn narration shift by 25 percentage points on average beyond the matched single-turn baseline. Stage-level analysis identifies preference optimization as a major contributor, while four inference-time strategies provide only partial mitigation. We hope our project fosters LLM advisors that preserve independent judgment in real-world consultation.

author: Saptarshi Basu, Sandeep Kakar, Ashok Goel
title: A Prompt-Engineering Approach to Develop Scalable, Flexible, and Real-Time Hybrid Micro-Level Personalization in a General Purpose AI Teaching Assistant
content:
arXiv:2609.03402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) teaching assistants powered by large language models (LLMs) offer scalable educational support but often provide limited personalization. This study presents a prompt-engineering-based framework for personalizing general-purpose LLM/RAG-based AI teaching assistants such as Jill Watson across academic disciplines and courses. The framework adapts responses using six learner-specific dimensions: self-assessment, abstraction preference, verbosity preference, perceptual orientation, information processing style, and level of understanding, yielding 96 distinct learner profiles. Student queries are additionally analyzed using Bloom's Taxonomy to estimate cognitive complexity at the interaction level. Learner attributes and cognitive assessments are encoded in structured prompts that condition the LLM without requiring model retraining. The framework is evaluated through experiments using NLP metrics and a human study with five participants. Results show perceived differences in response style and structure across personalization conditions, with statistical analyses identifying learner attributes associated with measurable response changes. These findings provide preliminary evidence that prompt-based personalization can support adaptive behavior in LLM-powered educational agents.

author: Evan Chen, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton
title: Fresh Memory, Stale Plans: Dependency-Scoped Validation for Distributed LLM-Agent Memory
content:
arXiv:2609.03340v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributed LLM-agent teams can read the latest shared facts and still act on an obsolete plan. A planner may derive an action from requirement $r_3$, another agent may commit $r_4$, and an executor may receive $r_4$ without replacing the plan derived from $r_3$. We call this \emph{stale-plan execution}: state freshness does not establish that the plan authorizing an action remains valid. We introduce PlanFence, a dependency-scoped action-validation protocol. Plans cite the exact public records they used, and an executor validates only the records that can affect the pending external action, replanning once or blocking when validation is incomplete. In 30 controlled live workflows with a post-plan revision, a freshness-only executor acts on the obsolete plan in every task, whereas PlanFence completes all tasks without an invalid action. Controlled replay reveals two conditional boundaries: proactive synchronization yields lower coordination stall at low churn, while PlanFence avoids repeated update-path coordination as churn grows and avoids validating unrelated state as the shared keyspace grows. These are controlled safety and systems-cost results, not general task-accuracy gains.

author: Zeyu Liu, Souvik Kundu, Peter A. Beerel
title: Speculative Macro Commit for Faster Tool-Using Agents
content:
arXiv:2609.03236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents spend wall-clock time not only on model inference but also in serial action--observation turns, where each tool call, environment transition, and observation can delay subsequent decisions. We introduce \textbf{Speculative Macro Commit} (SMC), a runtime mechanism for a two-tier agent system: a large authoritative actor model produces the official trajectory, while a faster speculative drafter model continuously predicts and executes future action chains on an isolated environment snapshot. SMC mines recurring multi-action skeletons from training traces and stores them in a macro library used to match against action chains predicted by the drafter at runtime. When the actor's next tool call matches the first drafted action, SMC commits the remaining pre-executed draft steps, together with their observations, to the official trajectory. Using Qwen3.5-27B INT4 as the authoritative actor model and Qwen3.5-4B as the speculative drafter model, SMC matches the sequential agent's overall accuracy while reducing latency by 10.23\% over the Speculative Actions (SA) baseline and 18.59\% over sequential execution on the $\tau^2$-Bench Telecom subset. On AppWorld, SMC reduces wall time by 7.7\% over SA baseline and 44.9\% over sequential execution, with a small reduction in task completion. Overall, SMC provides a practical way to reuse multi-step speculative execution and reduce agent latency beyond single-step speculative actions. Our code is publicly available \href{https://github.com/zeyuliu1037/speculative-macro-commit}{\textcolor{magenta}{here}}.

author: MasterControl AI Lab
title: MasterControl Seventeen Every Time
content:
arXiv:2609.03209v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a governed approach to enterprise analytics: a language model interprets the question, while deterministic policy selects and runs a pre-approved analytical program that returns both results and evidence. We show that this restriction can remain expressive within a defined analytical class, using relational operations plus aggregation, comparison, windows, ranking, and similarity. Fixed meaning, policy, data, and execution rules also make results replayable. Across 440 runs, three 8B models generated SQL and selected tools at runtime, while Qwen3-8B interpreted intent only and policy executed the approved program. None of 330 runtime-planning episodes matched the full answer-and-evidence contract across all test datasets; the policy-executed analyzer matched 110 of 110. This is a configuration-specific result, not evidence that runtime agents cannot succeed under other designs.

author: Ya Wang, Lei Zhang, Xueguang Yang, Bo Chen
title: Structure and Implementation of New Practical English Textbooks Driven by Artificial Intelligence
content:
arXiv:2609.02981v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing the form of applied English materials from fixed paper sequences to adaptive learning systems that can diagnose learners, recommend tasks, and provide formative feedback. This paper studies the structure and application of a new practical English textbook driven by artificial intelligence. A five-layer architecture is proposed: knowledge mapping, learner profiling, task generation, feedback orchestration, and teacher-side governance. A prototype was tested on 186 non-English-major undergraduates for eight weeks of teaching. Compared with a static digital textbook, the proposed system increased the unit completion accuracy from 72.4% to 84.9%, raised the average score for speaking tasks by 10.8 points, and reduced the teacher's correction time by 31.6%. Therefore, an AI-driven textbook can maintain the stability of the curriculum while providing personalised learning paths, rich practice materials and traceable classroom data.

2026年9月，柏林的初秋被雨水浸透，展览中心灰色的建筑群在晨光里安静展开，像一台刚启动的精密设备。在这座信奉“工程师文化”的城市，习惯用确定性和流程感丈量一切。
想看点不同寻常产品的人，来IFA会非常失望。
你看不到会飞的扫地机，场馆里也没有人形机器人做家务。大门外，招牌最醒目的仍然是赞助商常客TCL。
科技记者、自媒体人大概率会有些无聊，但如果你是个经销商、或者想为新家添置一些新家电，来这里一定能找到解决方案。
活动现场，我们随处可见带有IFA图标的彩色背板，“The future is now.”这句标语被挂在展馆的许多角落，字样格外显眼。
但IFA是个实用主义的展会。每台设备旁边都贴着技术参数卡和适用场景说明，法国用户手握着扫地机地盘，反复对比抹布结构差异，确认机械臂的实际作用；还有专门从荷兰、澳洲飞来的经销商围着一台割草机，半蹲下身研究底盘刀片。它是企业们做生意、找客户的场地，不是秀技术肌肉的展示台。
围观的人最爱问的只有一句话：你这个产品到底现在能解决什么问题？
所以，任何还想做海外市场的企业，不能也不敢缺席IFA。 根据IFA展会官方统计，今年共有928家中国内地企业参展，加上84家香港展商，中国参展商总数突破千家，在1900多家参展商中占比近半。这个数字同比2025年增长了近35%。它热度仍然很高，我们去德国参会的签证提前一个月跨城申请，而平常淡季，通常只需要半个月。
即便人潮涌动，这里还是少了一些新闻。不同于拉斯维加斯CES的兴奋和炫目，IFA的气质是另一种色彩，它严肃、克制、务实。在柏林这个古老的城市，举办了102年的IFA还是那样平静稳定，一切都不慌不忙。

IFA场馆外追觅广告大屏（图源/硬氪拍摄）
别聊AI和具身，告诉我怎么割草地
对穗升科技创始人王时远来说，IFA并不是陌生的战场。过去很多次，他是以安克高管的身份站在这里，熟稔地操盘着这套中国硬件出海不可缺席的标准打法。
直到2026年柏林，他换了一重完全不一样的身份，作为一家初创AI硬件公司的创始人，守在相比以往并不算大的展位上。
身份切换带来的视角冲击很强烈。他依旧能看到熟悉的展会喧嚣，也读出了完全不一样的市场信号。
欧洲似乎被抛在AI浪潮之后。一个很微妙的细节反复在展位上演：当他用国内惯常的话语体系聊AI Agent、Memory硬件概念时，现场观众的反应普遍迟缓，很难快速理解。他只能说：“这能用AI搭建一个属于你自己的全天知识库”，对方立刻开始追问具体怎么用、数据怎么存、能不能适配现有工作流。

穗升科技展台上，王时远与海外用户交流（图源/硬氪拍摄）
而国内追逐了整整两年的“具身智能”热潮，在IFA现场几乎找不到回声。
走进任何一个机器人品牌的展台，基本听不到世界模型、空间智能这类词汇。展台屏幕上循环播放的不是机器人翻跟头的炫酷动作，而是割草机在雨后湿滑的斜坡上停住、扫地机的机械臂探入桌椅腿缝隙、擦窗机器人紧贴弧形玻璃边缘滑过。
一位参展商半开玩笑地向硬氪总结道，“在深圳，你要是不在PPT里写两页‘具身智能’，投资人都不理你；但在柏林，你要是不把草坪割好，用户当场就走人。” 
这句话背后，是一整套关于技术叙事明显的区域性差异。
欧洲用户经历了一次身份转换。未岚大陆欧洲业务总经理Ryan Kong向硬氪表示，其人群属性正从“技术关注者”转变为“体验结果关注者”。
“现场用户的提问方式彻底改变，他们不再追问技术原理，而是细致到问每个零件怎么影响割完的草坪效果。”Ryan Kong说。
过去几年，割草机器人赛道迭代速度极快，每代产品都能带来肉眼可感知的体验升级。随着渗透率抬升，欧洲用户正逐步完成从“找产品”到“找体验”再到“找品牌”的认知演进。以德国为代表的高渗透率市场，已经率先进入第三阶段。

未岚大陆展台上的模拟草坪（图源/硬氪拍摄）
这种变化直接反映在今年的IFA展台设计上。未岚大陆不再只讲无边界、三合一导航这些概念，而是开始讲“刺猬”。在欧洲自然保护意识盛行的背景下，把“避开刺猬”纳入产品叙事，意味着品牌开始从技术参数的比拼转向满足当地的价值主张。
库犸则在展区梳理了一条十年四代产品的演进路径，直观展示每一代产品所解决的具体问题：能不能爬坡、会不会滑下来、边角能不能割干净。“用户先是学会了用真实使用效果评判产品好坏，然后才具备辨别品牌差异的能力。”库犸全球品牌负责人Angel表示。割草机器人的竞争，正在从技术参数的比拼转向体验承诺的交付。

库犸展出消费级及商用级割草机器人、泳池机器人（图源/硬氪拍摄）
耐士劳的展台叙事今年也发生明显转向，户外庭院生态微缩场景成为展示重点。割草机器人穿行于模拟果园，通过自主规划路径，展示复杂环境下的稳定定位与自主导航能力；

author: IT之家
title: 国内首台：我国自主研发危化防爆巡检无人机成功首飞，进入爆炸危险等级最高区域作业
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，据新华社报道，9 月 3 日，由西北工业大学、柔性电子全国重点实验室中国科学院黄维院士团队、北京航空航天大学等科研单位共同研发的国内首台防爆巡检无人机在山东成功首飞。
无人机全程自主完成厂区全覆盖巡检，同步检测危险气体泄漏、排查设备跑冒滴漏，顺利进入此前人工和普通无人机均无法抵达的爆炸危险等级最高区域作业。

IT之家从报道获悉，危化行业巡检长期面临两个难题：普通无人机进入易燃易爆厂区，电机火花、机身静电可能成为移动引爆源；加装厚重隔爆壳的改装机型，续航往往仅五六分钟，难以完成一次完整巡检。
研发团队首创正压惰性气体密封舱、隔爆电机、柔性检测传感器、静电导除四重闭环防爆架构，用主动隔绝可燃气体的方式替代被动防护，让无人机可进入氢气、乙炔泄漏的最高危险区域作业。机身贴敷的柔性电子传感器仅重 1.88 克，如同一层“电子皮肤”，能同时检测氢气、甲烷、一氧化碳、乙醇、VOC、甲醛等 13 种危险气体，实现毫秒级快速响应。
“这架无人机支持自主规划航线、自动起降回舱、24 小时无人值守巡检。”中国科学院院士黄维介绍，它的关键软硬件全部自主研发，元器件实现 100% 国产化，取得全国首张柔性气体探测防爆合格证，整机及核心部件均通过国家防爆标准检测，雨天、夜间、高温全场景可用，泄漏识别准确率 93%。

author: IT之家
title: 广汽集团：2021 年广汽资本参投长鑫科技，前瞻布局终获回报
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，9 月 4 日，广汽集团发文谈到了参投长鑫科技。早在 2021 年，广汽集团便通过旗下资本运营与投融资平台广汽资本，前瞻参与投资长鑫科技，打通了整车应用场景与上游芯片研发的协同通道，迈出了汽车芯片领域产业布局的关键一步。
IT之家从文章获悉，时间回拨到 2021 年，全球汽车行业正遭遇“缺芯”阵痛，芯片供给波动直接制约整车生产，供应链自主可控成为全行业共同面对的课题。面对挑战，广汽一方面全力克服芯片短缺影响，实现产销稳步增长；另一方面明确提出：加强芯片领域投资与产业链上下游合作，助力供应链自主可控，增强综合竞争力。
2021 年，广汽资本参投长鑫科技，正是这一战略思路下的重要落子。时隔五年，这份前瞻布局接连收获兑现：2026 年 7 月，长鑫科技正式登陆上交所科创板，创下 A 股年内最大 IPO 纪录；如今长鑫 LPDDR6 成功量产，更标志着国产存储芯片跻身全球第一梯队。
据广汽官方透露，近年来，广汽在芯片领域已累计投资超 29 家相关领域硬科技企业，覆盖芯片设计、晶圆制造、封装测试、车载终端应用全链条。此外，广汽围绕汽车产业未来趋势，先后投资地平线、粤芯半导体、小马智行、文远知行、清陶能源等超过 140 家优质企业，累计 49 家登陆资本市场。截至目前，已有 20 家参投企业上市。

author: IT之家
title: 奥尔特曼自曝是“超级果粉”，为苹果起诉 OpenAI 而感到难过
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，据《商业内幕》今天（5 日）报道，OpenAI CEO 萨姆 · 奥尔特曼一直是苹果的超级拥趸，但苹果起诉 OpenAI，让他的这份喜爱受到了“一次考验”。
奥尔特曼在接受科技记者亚历克斯 · 希思采访时坦言：“我算是苹果的超级铁粉，所以这件事让我很难过。”
今年 7 月，苹果对 OpenAI 提起诉讼，指控 OpenAI 为窃取苹果严密保护的商业秘密，在机构层面有组织地实施了一系列不当行为。OpenAI 否认对其他公司的商业秘密感兴趣，并称这起诉讼有负苹果“对最细微之处都反复推敲”的一贯声誉。
奥尔特曼表示，自己最初听说苹果起诉 OpenAI 时，还以为肯定出了非常严重的问题：“我第一次听说的时候心想，天啊，这听起来太恶劣了，肯定有人做了很糟糕的事。我们不想要任何公司的知识产权，当然也不希望有人把一家公司的知识产权带到我们这里。”
苹果最初提交的 40 页诉状几乎没有提及奥尔特曼。除若干企业实体外，苹果直接列为被告的 OpenAI 员工只有曾在苹果供职的 Chang Liu 和 Tang Tan。苹果指控两人在离职时带走或保留了机密信息，某些情况下还曾向仍在苹果任职的员工询问尚未发布的产品。
这起诉讼也标志着苹果与 OpenAI 的关系发生重大转折。2024 年 6 月，奥尔特曼还曾前往库比蒂诺宣布，苹果将在旗下产品中整合 ChatGPT。
此后，OpenAI 开始进入苹果长期占据优势的消费市场，双方的合作关系逐渐恶化。在苹果全球开发者大会上发言不到一年后，奥尔特曼与 iPhone 设计师乔尼 · 艾维宣布，两人已合作多年，OpenAI 还将以近 65 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 437.38 亿元人民币）收购艾维创办的初创公司 IO。
奥尔特曼长期以来从不掩饰自己对苹果的喜爱。2008 年，他曾在苹果全球开发者大会上演示自己共同创办的基于位置的社交应用 Loopt。奥尔特曼表示，当时想登上大会舞台，需要得到苹果 CEO 史蒂夫 · 乔布斯批准。他后来把这次经历称为自己职业生涯的高光时刻，也是自己在商业活动中“唯一一次紧张到那种程度”。
2015 年，奥尔特曼回忆自己从小就把乔布斯视为偶像级人物时表示：“那可是史蒂夫 · 乔布斯，你懂的。”奥尔特曼的第一台电脑是 Macintosh LC II。2024 年，他告诉比尔 · 盖茨，这台电脑仍在自己手中，而且还能正常运行。
宣布与艾维合作时，奥尔特曼表示：“希望重现我 30 年前第一次使用苹果电脑时感受到的那份愉悦、惊奇和创造精神”。
去年 11 月，奥尔特曼与艾维和劳伦 · 鲍威尔 · 乔布斯同台对谈时，将 iPhone 称为“消费产品的巅峰之作”。
奥尔特曼不持有 OpenAI 股权，其财富主要来自对 Stripe、Reddit 等公司的投资。他最早的科技投资之一，可能就来自祖母的一份生日礼物。
奥尔特曼与兄弟杰克在 2016 年的一次访谈中回忆，每逢生日，祖母都会给两人价值相同的公司股票，挑选她认为他们会喜欢的公司。杰克拿到的是 Applebee's 股票，萨姆拿到的则是苹果股票。“时至今日，我的证券账户里还把那些苹果股票标记为‘祖母送的生日苹果股票’。我会一直留着它们。”

author: IT之家
title: 两家美国媒体起诉 OpenAI 和微软，指控其 AI 训练侵犯版权
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，据路透社报道，《西雅图时报》与《新闻日报》于本周五（9 月 4 日）正式起诉 OpenAI 与微软。两家美国媒体指控 OpenAI 与微软未经授权擅自复制其新闻报道，用于训练旗下 AI。
该诉讼已提交至美国纽约南区联邦地区法院。起诉书指出，OpenAI 和微软抓取了两家媒体的网站内容，其中包含付费墙背后的专属内容；随后，这些文章被直接整合入训练数据集，用于训练和驱动 ChatGPT、微软 Copilot 以及必应的 AI 检索等功能。
两家媒体表示，涉案公司的 AI 产品不仅能完整复现报道中的原文段落，还能进行高度雷同的文本改写，并直接为用户提供综合答案。这极大削弱了读者访问媒体官网或付费订阅的必要性。
OpenAI 发言人回应称，其模型均基于公开数据训练，并符合合理使用原则，但未对本次诉讼的具体指控置评。
微软发言人则在电子邮件中表示：“尽管这起诉讼令我们感到意外，但我们高度认可地方新闻报道的重要性。我们始终愿意与各方坦诚沟通，共同寻求解决此类纠纷的方案。”
IT之家获悉，《西雅图时报》和《新闻日报》正寻求法院发布命令，要求相关公司全面销毁所侵权作品的副本，以及任何包含这些内容的训练数据集和 AI 模型。

author: IT之家
title: 捷豹路虎即将启动大裁员，消息称总数达 4000 人
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，据《泰晤士报》今天（5 日）报道，英国最大汽车制造商捷豹路虎汽车计划未来两年裁员 4000 人，以应对成本飙升、销量大幅下滑以及美国关税带来的压力。
当地时间周五晚些时候，消息称捷豹路虎已向员工发出预警，公司预计将在下周一公布裁员计划。
捷豹路虎向彭博社作出回应称，公司将启动自愿离职计划，目标是在未来两年节省约 17 亿英镑（IT之家注：现汇率约合 154.46 亿元人民币）。面对全球市场环境变化，捷豹路虎希望将盈亏平衡销量降至 30 万辆，同时精简业务。不过，捷豹路虎没有在声明中透露计划裁减的具体人数。

捷豹路虎在英国拥有约 3.3 万名员工，由印度塔塔汽车乘用车有限公司控股。最近一个季度，公司营收下降近 10%，税前利润大跌 69% 至 1.09 亿英镑（现汇率约合 9.9 亿元人民币）。
本月早些时候，捷豹路虎首款纯电动揽胜上市，售价 15.407 万英镑（现汇率约合 140 万元人民币），是目前市场上价格最高的电动 SUV 之一，比对应的燃油车型贵近 5 万英镑（现汇率约合 45.4 万元人民币）。这样的定价也进一步拉大了纯电动揽胜与席卷英国市场的中国低价 SUV 之间的价格差距。
除成本和销量压力外，捷豹路虎还面临美国关税上升以及中国市场需求下滑的压力。去年，公司曾遭遇网络攻击，全球业务一度全面停摆。
关税环境以及中国电动汽车带来的竞争压力，同样困扰着其他欧洲汽车制造商。大众汽车集团监事会支持一项重组计划，其中包括再裁员 5 万人。

author: IT之家
title: 美政府移民主题游戏借鉴《俄罗斯方块》玩法，后者版权方声明“与我无关”
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，9 月 4 日，俄罗斯方块公司在 Instagram 发表声明称，美国政府新推出的移民主题游戏《Build the Wall》并非由该公司参与制作。这款游戏是白宫周四发布的 6 款新街机游戏之一，玩法明显仿照《俄罗斯方块》。

俄罗斯方块公司在声明中称：“我们相信，俄罗斯方块拥有连接人与人、让大家走到一起的力量。致世界各地的玩家：我们爱你们，我们看见你们，也感谢你们成为这个社区的一员。我们没有参与《Build the Wall》的制作，并且非常严肃地对待侵版问题。”

IT之家注：俄罗斯方块公司是负责《俄罗斯方块》品牌全球授权事务的管理机构，由俄罗斯方块创始人阿列克谢 · 帕基特诺夫与亨克 · 罗杰斯共同持有。公司也是“Tetris Holding LLC”的独家被授权方，后者拥有俄罗斯方块在全球范围内的完整版权。
《Build the Wall》的玩法是把不断落下的砖块堆叠并嵌入一堵持续升高的墙，与《俄罗斯方块》十分相似。区别在于，玩家即使拼出完整的一行，砖块也不会被消除，墙体只会越来越高，用来阻挡不断逼近的“僵尸群”。游戏中的墙体又被设置在一个界定模糊的“南部边境”附近，使其反移民立场更加明确。
俄罗斯方块公司在回应外媒 Engadget 置评请求时再次强调，公司没有参与《Build the Wall》的制作，也没有授权或许可该游戏使用《俄罗斯方块》品牌或知识产权。“40 多年来，《俄罗斯方块》一直通过游戏和乐趣，让不同世代和文化背景的人走到一起。这款游戏的目标始终是有目的地堆叠方块，尽可能消除更多行。我们目前正在审查此事。”

author: IT之家
title: 塔塔咨询将在印度海得拉巴建设 1GW AI 数据中心，预计投资 7000 亿卢比
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，塔塔咨询服务公司今日宣布，旗下子公司 HyperVault 已取得 264 英亩（约 106.9 公顷）土地，计划在印度海得拉巴打造规划容量高达 1 吉瓦（1GW）的大规模 AI 数据中心园区。
官方表示，该数据中心可支持面向 AI 模型训练、推理以及复杂高性能计算工作负载的高密度 GPU 部署。建设将采取分期推进策略，密切匹配客户算力需求与底层技术迭代要求。全面建成后，该园区预计将跻身印度规模最大、技术最先进的 AI 基础设施园区之列。
项目落地后，预计将在当地创造数千个直接与间接就业岗位。HyperVault 及其合作伙伴预计将投资高达 7,000 亿印度卢比（IT之家注：现汇率约合 497.87 亿元人民币），用于该算力基础设施的建设与长期运营。
IT之家注意到，保时捷于当地时间 8 月 24 日，与塔塔咨询签署了一项为期五年、价值 12.5 亿欧元（现汇率约合 97.6 亿元人民币）的 AI 合作协议。塔塔咨询称将为保时捷实现“规模化、工业级的 AI 技术落地”。

title: 蔚来：长三角地区全面实现换电县县通，累计建成 1412 座换电站
content:
IT之家 9 月 5 日消息，蔚来官方今日宣布，黄山祁门低碳科创园蔚来换电站上线，蔚来能源正式实现安徽换电县县通，这也意味着长三角地区全面实现换电县县通。蔚来能源在安徽已累计建成 216 座换电站，覆盖全省 104 个区县，每个区县都有蔚来换电站。
在长三角地区，蔚来能源已累计建成 1,412 座换电站，覆盖 303 个区县，打通长三角城市群高速换电网络，布局 289 座高速公路换电站，平均不到 100 公里就有一座蔚来换电站。

IT之家获悉，蔚来能源已在全国建成 1,052 座高速公路换电站，打通 9 纵 11 横 16 大城市群高速换电网络，连通全国超 550 城。
截至目前，蔚来在全国已累计建成充换电站 9,317 座，其中换电站 4,067 座、充电站 5,250 座、充电桩 30,272 根。

author: 36氪
title: 硬氪首发 | 解决钙钛矿材料涂布难题，中科院系企业完成数千万元Pre-A轮融资
content:
作者｜乔钰杰
编辑｜袁斯来
本文1500字，预计阅读4分钟
硬氪获悉，钙钛矿太阳能电池企业长春日耀光电科技有限公司（以下简称“日耀光电”）完成数千万元Pre-A轮融资，由天津创业投资管理有限公司（天创资本）与吉林省科技投资基金有限公司（吉林省科投）联合出资。此前，公司曾获长兴基金数千万元天使轮独家投资。
日耀光电成立于2023年，依托中国科学院长春应用化学研究所秦川江研究员团队的研究成果创立，团队在Science、Nature等期刊累计发表论文110余篇。公司目前布局新型自组装分子（SAM分子）材料、薄膜在线检测装备、钙钛矿太阳能电池组件三大产品线。
SAM材料是日耀光电的核心突破口。该材料主要用作钙钛矿电池的空穴传输层。团队开发的新型自由基SAM分子，通过独特的分子设计在结构中引入官能团或扭转构型，显著提升其在溶液中的分散性，在国际上首次解决了SAM薄膜的大面积涂布难题。

（图源/企业）
目前，钙钛矿电池产线普遍采用氧化镍（NiOx）作为空穴传输层，再叠加钝化层材料，工序复杂、成本较高。日耀光电开发的SAM材料可实现无NiOx的大面积制备新工艺，改进产线结构，使产线投资成本减少20%、电池制造成本降低10%。
基于这一自主SAM材料，公司与隆基合作、经NREL认证的钙钛矿/晶硅叠层电池效率达34.2%，处于世界前三水平。目前，核心SAM材料已与国内外100余家企业及科研机构开展合作。
检测装备方面，秦川江告诉硬氪：“只有2–3纳米厚的SAM薄膜，要表征它的物理化学性能非常难，目前市面上没有商业化装备能全方面评价这一层性能的好坏。”
基于这一痛点，日耀光电首创SAM原位表征技术，合作开发出一体化检测装备，可实现原位、高精度、多模态、高通量的材料筛选与产线在线检测。该装备基于电化学原理，能够有效表征薄膜的物理化学特性，填补了钙钛矿电池生产过程中的工艺监测缺口。目前设备正在进行商品化迭代。
电池组件方面，团队可自主完成从材料到组件的全流程开发，目前最大可制备300×300毫米尺寸器件。未来，公司产品将主要面向车载光伏与空天光伏两大方向。
本轮融资资金将重点用于建设国内首条年产百公斤级新型自组装空穴传输材料中试线，扩充核心研发团队；同时建设大尺寸钙钛矿电池组件试验线，锁定车载光伏与空天光伏两大应用赛道。
以下为硬氪与日耀光电创始团队交流节选：
硬氪：钙钛矿量产化的最大瓶颈是大面积制备，大面积涂布的难点具体在哪一层？日耀光电的SAM材料解决了什么问题？
秦川江：我们的材料相当于钙钛矿电池底部的第一层功能层，涂在导电基底上。现在主流的产线工艺，是在ITO导电玻璃上先镀一层氧化镍，再在氧化镍上涂布钝化材料或直接做钙钛矿，我们的材料是在钙钛矿之前直接涂布。
大面积组件的难点在于，每一层都必须足够好，最终才能得到高效率的器件。这也是为什么小面积器件效率可以很高，而大面积组件效率还达不到晶硅的水平。我们这层SAM材料首先解决的是空穴传输层本身的质量，同时它也会直接影响上面钙钛矿层的成膜质量。更重要的是，它让空穴传输层实现了无氧化镍制备，省掉了一层工艺。
硬氪：现阶段收入来自SAM材料和检测装备，未来再切组件，这个节奏是如何考量的？
秦川江：我们目前的定位是上游材料与工艺供应商，和下游主机厂之间不存在直接竞争，这让我们更容易获得业内认可。先做材料和检测装备，本质上是在钙钛矿产业化的最上游先卡住位置，这个阶段比拼的是技术和材料性能，而不是组件产能。
当然，我们也要考虑客户未来自行开发同类材料的风险，所以会通过持续的技术迭代保持领先。
组件方面，我们现在已经能够小批量制作。至于大规模组件产线要不要建、什么时候建，会根据市场的发展情况来决定。如果钙钛矿市场很快起来，且市场空间足够大，我们也有可能搭建组件产线，这属于公司的长期战略选项。

author: 36氪
title: 那些「不日常」的衣服，买了到底要穿去哪？
content:
01 不日常单品，年轻人留给生活的彩蛋
女生的衣柜总是不够用的，倒不是因为真的缺衣服，只是女孩们总在尝试风格变换，而每种风格的自己都想拥有一件对应的搭配。
衣柜里总是会住进不少心血来潮拍下的单品，它们往往没那么日常，但在你付款的那一刻，就已经被安排好未来的出场剧本。这是年轻女孩们留给自己的生活彩蛋，有这样一件单品在，打开衣柜，就总会唤起那颗向往“非日常情景”的、躁动的心。
比如，一条黄色波点丝巾。下单时，脑内已经闪过一张自带法式滤镜的城市户外画布，你会在某个周末的傍晚，搭一件简单的素色背心和轻薄防风外套，徐徐漫步在铺满梧桐叶的大道上，享受夕阳、夜色和晚风。

George Shervashidze，图源Pexels
一双方头芭蕾鞋。它看起来温柔，但加入了利落的鞋型和一点结构感后就更带点雷厉风行。你会想象自己穿着简约的直筒牛仔裤和白色短袜，外面罩一件短风衣，去看一场盛大的戏剧。在散场后沿着剧场外的小路慢慢走，像带上了舞台的轻盈，从梦幻的幕布下走回城市的真实。

Jennie的芭蕾风穿搭
一条流行的流苏半裙。买下它时，心里已经摆好pose，那是个完整的画面：黑色背心外搭做旧牛仔外套，裙摆随着步子晃出一点西部感。你会到livehouse台下，跟随着DJ的节奏感挥手尽情摇摆，身上的流苏负责记录下形体的律动。

Raimonda Kulikauskiene/Getty Images
一件款式颇具设计感的文胸。收货时就在想它的几十种花式搭配了，你想象它叠在薄纱般的皮肤衣外，成为整套OOTD里最C位的元素，或者仅仅是穿着文胸，披一件机车风外套，自然衬出身形，大大方方展示自己。它的出场画面更具体，是在万人尽情热舞的广场上，在音乐节的聚光灯下，你会是人群中的焦点。


图源爱慕品牌官方
这就是“不日常单品”的魔力——购买它的那一刻，你已经提前畅想到某种精彩的特殊场合，仅仅是拥有它们，就是在保存对生活在别处的想象。
这些念头往往来得很随机，尤其是当人被眼前的日常困住时。加班到焦头烂额时，屏幕上的文档还没改完，脑子就情不自禁飞到某个叫不上名字的欧洲小镇，想着自己该挑个时间规划一段solotrip了；在图书馆里准备考试时，上一秒还在背题，下一秒已经规划着跟朋友们去那家精致的小酒馆出片，该换一套新的造型。


图源爱慕品牌官方
而两点一线的通勤地铁上，最容易冒出这样的想法：好像突然切换到“穿搭观察”模式，看着车厢里人们的造型，就脑补着他们要去怎样的场合经营新的一天，结果自己也打开了购物网站，加购了几件一直没舍得买的衣服。下一次，不要再穿着它挤在人群里赶路了，要留给一场没有目的地的citywalk。
这些开小差的时候，买下的不止是一件不日常的单品，而是未来出门的dress code。这些漂亮衣服，其实一直藏在衣柜里等待被穿出门的时刻，那不一定有多隆重，而是，它们在等待你允许“不日常”发生的那个契机。
02 当内衣不再只负责“隐身”
阿那亚的海滩总是有种褪色的恬淡，浅色沙子、灰蓝海面、白色围栏，它在等待几抹亮色点缀的时刻。那往往是特殊场合到来的时刻——在刚过去的周末，虾米音乐节选在这片海滩上举办。
这样的集体狂欢，年轻人们早就呼唤已久，她们也许提前多时就在衣柜里备好了整身搭配，为展示出自己最闪亮的一面。
海滩上，绑着蓝色头巾的女孩着一身透感长袖，把牛仔款拉链文胸穿在最外层，白色蕾丝裙和麂皮靴的化学反应衬得她像一位优雅的流浪诗人；

有人腰间随手系一件蓝衬衫，脚下踩一双麂皮长靴，像刚从公路电影里穿越来了海边；也有人用米色钩针开衫叠穿同色系短上衣，肩上松松披一件廓形外套，倚靠在镜子前，带了一丝洒脱不羁。


风格不一、自在随性的女性们，共同构成了海滩音乐节特有的时尚感，拼接成一副活力洋溢的画面。
这样的甜酷女孩们，尤其聚集在海滩边一座红色格调的店面前。“爱慕封面影棚”快闪店，这里的她们都有着共同的穿搭元素——封面文胸，这就是一种“不日常单品”的露出。


虾米音乐节“爱慕封面影棚”快闪店
有简约风格的穿搭——直接穿一身白色，衬衫自然敞开当外套，下摆松松搭在白色长裙外，封面文胸和脚上的黑色牛仔靴共同构成核心视觉因素；同样的黑色款也能穿得温婉优雅，白色系带开衫在胸前打了个结，下身配黑白波点半裙，头发利落地梳到脑后。
两套look都是无彩色穿搭的教科书示例，黑白配难免单调，封面文胸带来的适度露肤恰好对冲了无趣感，可以是松弛里带一点帅气的浪漫，也可以是优雅里不失随性洒脱。


棕色款也能被诠释出两种脾气。搭做旧牛仔外套和浅色牛仔短裤时，外套半垮在肩上，手插在兜里，是美式复古那股劲；换到米色钩针开衫和白色长裤里，又突然温柔下来——钩花的镂空和胸前的交叉绑带叠在一起，有一种安静的、度假式的慵懒。


这确实和大家熟悉的那个老牌爱慕有些不一样了。
今年8-9月，爱慕的秋上新

author: 36氪
title: Agent做医生“首席助理”：看片速度快，人机协作仍是最优解
content:
近日，第五届医学影像AI学术会议在上海举办。现场，一场公开的“人机读片大赛”成为会议讨论焦点。
在国内，AI医学影像企业一贯喜欢举办“人类VS人工智能”的读片大赛，展示自家AI的“判断力”。但这次，不同于行业常见的内部测评，会议主办方从各地三甲医院中征集了10份“令医生们觉得‘见所未见’”的真实影像病例，设置7类“医生+AI协作”或AI智能体独立写作的参赛组，由这些参赛选手们提前完成10份诊断报告撰写，再让医生专家现场打分，直观体现报告质量与产出效率的真实差异。
把模型直接放到几十位顶尖专家眼皮底下实时实战，极具压力。毕竟，每一份输出报告都会被放大审视。AI参赛方数坤科技对36氪提到，这是一场“闭卷考试”。“组委没有告诉我们病例的具体情况，AI没有办法提前学习。参赛前，我们也很紧张，不知道它的表现会如何。”

赛后，数坤科技独立参赛的CT全胸智能体和DR全身智能体获大会颁发的“见所未见·勇气证书”
从现场公示结果来看，高年资医生加多任务智能体的组合平均得分最高，为85.2分；低年资医生加智能体的组合得分为83.8分，在部分病例中甚至拿到了全场最高分。独立工作的智能体得分为66.2分，在得分上逊于医生独立撰写和人机协作的形式，但用时仅20分32秒，是所有组别中最快的（各组用时均在66-88分钟之间）。

7组参赛选手撰写10份诊断报告的用时和得分情况（其中“低资”“高资”分别指代低年资医生和高年资医生）
一位被分到用传统病例模板“手搓”的低年资参赛医生坦言，脱离AI工具，依靠传统模板书写报告时，低年资医生往往会暴露经验短板，容易在病灶识别、征象定性的环节出现疏漏，报告整体质量波动较大。当前，这也是国内大量基层、年轻放射医师普遍面临的工作现状。
而搭配多任务智能体协同作业的组别中，医生可以拿到AI初步梳理完成的征象清单和报告初稿，病灶检出的覆盖度更高，能够减少人眼阅片带来的漏检风险。
不过，新的实操问题随之显现，智能体输出的内容会混杂部分假阳性结果，医生需要逐一回到原始影像做复核校验，当AI给出的判断逻辑和自身临床认知不一致时，又需要投入额外时间做甄别判断，在部分病例上反而拉长了整体工作时长。“现阶段，临床中缺少明确的AI操作规范，我们该如何采信AI输出内容、如何把握边界？这也是一线日常工作里很实际的难题。”
与此同时，比赛中还有个有趣的现象：多位评审专家在解读打分结果时，都误判了报告来源。比如，有专家因为某份报告“写法和用词太熟悉了”，断定是高年资医生使用传统模板完成的，实际却是高年资医生使用垂直AI模型写出来的。这意味着，现阶段，AI生成的报告在术语和结构上已经越来越接近人类医生的表达习惯，人机边界慢慢变得模糊。
这场实测之所以备受会议现场的企业和医生关注，是因为它发生在医学影像行业技术迭代的关键节点。
过去数年，国内AI医学影像企业主要深耕垂直模型，一款模型聚焦单一任务，肺结节、冠脉、脑出血等各自对应独立产品，解决特定病灶检出、量化测量问题，不少产品拿到医疗器械注册证，已经进入医院落地使用；但垂直模型的局限性也逐步暴露。比如，放射科一份CT报告需要覆盖全身多器官、数十类异常征象，医生需要在多个AI模块间来回跳转调用，工具碎片化，很难贴合放射科完整的报告工作流。
伴随着大语言模型技术的渗透，近一两年，国内多家医疗影像厂商集体转向多模态、医疗智能体方向，尝试把分散的单任务模型整合起来，模拟放射医生完整阅片逻辑，实现一次影像输入，完成多器官多病种分析，直接生成完整报告初稿。
本次会议期间，数坤科技也发布了CT全胸、DR全身两款临床智能体产品，正是这一轮技术转向下的产物。另据数坤科技创始人、董事长毛新生透露，公司还将于近期“发布医学世界模型”。
行业普遍的期待是，把医生从重复的征象罗列、测量、初稿撰写工作释放出来，工作重心转向复核和综合研判。但技术概念落地到真实临床环境，效果往往和演示环境存在落差，这次“人机大赛”，正是希望将把这种落差完整呈现出来。
毛新生认为，上一代垂直模型擅长做“识别”类任务，经过标注数据训练，能完成病灶检测、分割、量化，能力边界清晰，优点是可控性强，缺点是任务能力固化，每新增一类疾病，就要重新做数据标注、训练新模型，很难泛化处理临床里层出不穷的非典型、少见病例；而大模型带来的变化是，模型具备了推理、归纳、组织语言的能力，不再仅仅输出病灶坐标与测量数值，而是能模仿放射诊断思维，完成阅片流程拆解、征象归纳、组织完整医学文本，有能力打通从影像信号到最终报告的全链路。
如果给两代技术打个比方，过去的AI就像“专科实习生”，只能看一种病，还需要医生手把手带。今天的AI智能体是更像是“首席助理”，把一张片子丢过去后，它能自己分诊、自己标注、自己写报告初稿，医生只需要审核签字。
这种变化带来的直接结果是工作流的重构：医生从

author: 36氪
title: IFA 2026前线｜蓝海赛道下的内卷现实，科沃斯如何回答全球化与具身智能考题
content:
作者｜黄楠
编辑｜袁斯来
2026年柏林，IFA 2026展会现场，家用机器人成为中国硬件军团的一大看点。扫拖地、擦窗、庭院割草、泳池维护等多品类机器人集中展出，覆盖场景从室内延伸至户外，从地面拓展至立面与水面。
其布局变化也折射出整个家用机器人行业近年来的演变趋势，从单一品类的纵深突破，走向全场景、多品类的平台化竞争。
当地时间9月3日，IFA开幕前一天，福布斯行业评估报告发布，正式将科沃斯评定为全球NO.1家用机器人品牌，综合得分8.56分。这份评定不只看市场份额，它考察的是一个更完整的维度，全球化运营的纵深、多品类商业化的落地能力、从上游供应链到下游品牌端的技术与渠道壁垒。
放眼全球大盘，家用服务机器人的增长逻辑依旧成立。IDC报告数据预测，2026年中国清洁机器人市场规模接近34亿美元，同比增长18%。其中，中国厂商出货量占全球份额85%以上，从供应链到产品定义，中国硬件公司正在深度主导这条赛道。
国内市场的现实体感形成反差。2026上半年，国内扫地机器人销额同比下滑4.0%，销量同比下滑4.6%。
一边是长期广阔的增量空间，一边是国内市场短期遇冷、成本抬升的现实压力。国内家庭扫地机器人渗透率仅5-7%，已经被充分教育的存量用户成为争夺的核心。
在这一背景下，2026年上半年，科���斯实现营收利润双位数增长，总营收达103.41亿元，同比增长19.18%；净利润12.48亿元，同比增长27.40%。

科沃斯扫地机器人在IFA 2026上展出（图源/企业）
财报数字的背后，科沃斯的解法落在三个相互关联的方向：加快业务重心在海外市场布局、复用成熟技术栈拓展家庭多场景硬件、搭建完整技术底座去迎接物理AI时代。
海外业务是支撑科沃斯本轮增长最核心的变量。数据显示，科沃斯上半年海外收入占品牌总营收49.0%，二季度首次突破51.0%，这是品牌成立近三十年来海外收入首次反超国内。
具体业务端，科沃斯主品牌海外营收同比上涨46.5%，添可海外营收同比增长40.6%；擦窗、割草、泳池机器人等新兴品类海外增速尤为突出，营收同比增幅达到75.1%。
海外市场的爆发不是短期流量红利，真正的全球化不等于“把货卖出去”，而是产品、供应链、服务整套体系适配全球市场。
2015年前后，科沃斯确立了产品本地化思路，针对不同地区的住宅环境和使用习惯进行定制化适配，并将其形成了一套“3S”技术框架，即Space（空间感知）、Setting（场景理解）和Service（服务交付）。
科沃斯集团副董事长、科沃斯机器人CEO钱程在IFA 2026演讲中指出，第一层是空间感知；机器人需要具备基础的感知能力，借助雷达与传感器技术，以厘米级、毫米级的精度对室内外环境进行测量与建图，这是后续一切决策的前提。

科沃斯集团副董事长、科沃斯机器人CEO钱程（图源/企业）
第二层是场景理解。室内与室外、厨房与卧室、有无宠物的家庭，不同空间对机器人的任务要求截然不同。当AI识别出地板上的污渍或家中有宠物时，扫地机会自动调整清洁策略，提升吸力或切换清扫模式。场景感知能力让机器人从“执行指令”进化到“理解环境”，并根据环境变化自主调整行为。
第三层是服务交付。空间与场景的认知不止于室内。户外草坪在不同地区差异，比如欧洲南部的草种与北欧不同，美国与澳大利亚的草坪养护习惯也各有特点；泳池的形态��材质、布局同样千差万别。只有深入理解这些细分场景的具体差异，才能为不同市场提供真正适配的产品与服务。
全球化打开外部增长空间，而同源技术驱动的多品类布局，则挖掘家庭内部的增量。
科沃斯的品类扩张并非无逻辑跨界。扫地机器人迭代十年沉淀下的感知、导航、避障、运动控制能力，正在被系统性地复用到更多家庭任务中。
窗宝是这套复用逻辑下最先跑通的品类。扫地机在地面识别障碍物的避障算法，被迁移至立面场景用于识别窗框、把手与玻璃边缘；应对地毯和门槛的越障动力，则复用为窗宝爬坡和跨越窗框的控制基础。这套迁移支撑窗宝连续三年全球市场第一，拿下65%的市占率，2025年销量突破100万台，2026上半年已成为百万级独立品类。
同样，割草机器人GOAT将室内复杂家居环境下的导航避障能力，迁移至开放庭院，从识别地面数据线、宠物粪便，延展为识别树木、花坛和户外家具；SLAM算法从室内二维地图升级为庭院三维建模。泳池机器人ULTRAMARINE则将路径规划算法从泳池水面迁移至水下环境，避障逻辑复用自窗宝对立面异形结构的识别经验。

科沃斯割草机器人GOAT（图源/企业）
三个新品类，共享同一个技术底座。从地面到立面、庭院、泳池，科沃斯完成的是技术能力的横向迁移，而非盲目的品类堆叠。
但家用机器人的想象空间远不止工具，具身智能落地正在重写人们的想象边界。
科沃斯正基于服务机器人测试其自研的“世界模型”，大模型承担人机交

author: 36氪
title: BP海投了三个月，投资人还是不知道你干什么
content:
项目很多，真正容易被读懂的并不多
今天缺的不是创业项目。新产品、新技术、新品牌、新模式每天都在出现。对投资人、产业方和潜在客户来说，信息越多，筛选越贵。他们真正要判断的，从来不是你讲得激不激动，而是这几个更硬的问题：这个问题是否真实存在？客户为什么非用你不可？产品已经验证到哪一步？和市场上已有方案相比，差异是不是可被理解的？团队凭什么有机会把这件事做成？
现实里，不少团队不是没有内容，是内容散在各处。技术放在一堆参数里，客户案例埋在聊天记录里，进展写在内部周报里，商业逻辑只存在创始人脑子里。对外一讲，要么过技术、要么过愿景，就是过不了“让人一次看懂”这一关。
有的项目把篇幅堆在技术细节上，商业价值却没讲清；有的已经有付费客户，材料里却拼不出完整业务闭环；还有的其实到了阶段性进展，只因为缺少一次公开、克制、专业的表达，行业外部很难建立认知。价值和表达之间，隔着一道很难自己跨过去的沟。「项目推荐」要做的，就是把这道沟填短：不是帮你编一个更响的故事，而是把已经存在的产品、客户、进展和判断，整理成符合行业阅读习惯的内容。

title: Protecting Dynamic Industrial Robot Cable Carriers
content:
This article is brought to you by Tsubaki KabelSchlepp.
In modern automated manufacturing, six-axis articulated robots perform high-speed, multidirectional maneuvers under demanding operational cycles. However, as robot arms swivel, rotate, and extend, the electrical cables, fiber optics, and pneumatic hoses supplying them endure severe mechanical stress. Torsional twist, rapid acceleration, and repeated contact with machine structures often lead to premature conductor fatigue, insulation breakdown, and costly unplanned production halts.
To overcome these multi-axis motion challenges, the Tsubaki KabelSchlepp Robotrax System provides a specialized three-dimensional cable carrier engineered specifically for complex robotic motion.
Managing High Tensile Forces With Central Steel Technology
Conventional cable carriers often transfer operational movement stress directly onto internal electrical lines and hoses. The Robotrax system changes this dynamic through a central steel cable that runs through the core of every chain link.
The Robotrax system’s central steel cable absorbs the primary tensile loads and preserves conductor integrity, dramatically extending cable service life.
When robot arms undergo rapid directional shifts and accelerations up to 10 g, this internal steel cable absorbs the primary tensile loads. By isolating electrical and fluid lines from pulling forces, the design preserves conductor integrity and dramatically extends cable service life. Mechanics can easily calibrate and adjust system tension using an integrated clamping piece, ensuring consistent mechanical support throughout long operational cycles.

author: Richard Mitchell
title: AI Efficiency Could Cost Us the Next Generation of Experts
content:
A little over a decade ago, I led the controls design for a first-of-its-kind full digital-control system for a U.S. nuclear plant. It was, on paper, a beautiful machine—engineered to run itself the way a modern airliner does, with operators watching over a system that rarely needed them. And we made a decision that, to an efficiency-minded observer, looked backward: We deliberately left manual steps inside sequences the system could execute on its own.

We were solving a specific problem. An operator who only ever supervises automation slowly stops being an operator. The hands go cold. The mental model of what the plant is actually doing gets fuzzy. Then comes the day the automation hands control back. It’s always the worst day, because automation only quits when it’s confused or in trouble. But by then, you have a person in the chair who hasn’t truly operated the thing in years. The manual steps were there to keep the human current. It was inefficient by design, on purpose.
That plant, as it happened, was never built. It was shelved amid the politics and economics that surround nuclear power in this country, for reasons that had nothing to do with the engineering. But the design instinct outlived the project, and I’ve come to believe it’s the most useful idea I can offer to the argument now consuming every boardroom: What happens to human expertise when AI does the work that used to build it?

author: Joanna Goodrich
title: NASA’s Cargo-Moving Robotic Arm Named 300th IEEE Milestone
content:
In the 1960s NASA began developing a system of reusable space shuttles to make its work more efficient and to reduce costs. The shuttles could launch like rockets, maneuver in Earth’s orbit, and land like airplanes. They also could carry large satellites to and from orbit.
Like other types of transportation, machinery eventually breaks down, and parts need to be replaced or fixed. And the cargo being carried to and from Earth has to be moved to its final destination. To complete such tasks, Spar Aerospace (now part of MDA Space) of Brampton, Ont., Canada, and the National Research Council in Ottawa developed a robotic arm, the Shuttle Remote Manipulator System. The project was a joint venture between the U.S. and Canadian governments.
Known as Canadarms, the robotic tools attached to shuttles’ exteriors. They allowed astronauts to handle and transfer tools, satellites, and other payloads. Inspections of the shuttle and repairs could be completed using the robots.
The system was first deployed in 1981 aboard Columbia’s second flight. Canadarm was used for 30 years on five shuttles and on the International Space Station.
The robotic arm was dedicated on 19 June as the 300th IEEE Milestone. The ceremony was held at MDA Space headquarters. The IEEE Toronto Section sponsored the nomination.
“It is appropriate that the 300th Milestone is the Canadarm,” says Michael Geselowitz, senior director of the IEEE History and Heritage group. “The technology spans aerospace, robotics, and computing fields of interest. title: Applying Different Forms of Mentorship
content:
This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!
Asking someone to be your mentor is weird. 
Walking up to someone and asking, “Will you be my mentor?” has always seemed to me like the adult version of a kid walking up to another kid at a party and asking, “Will you be my friend?”
What you’re really asking is: “Will you commit some amount of unpaid time to guiding my career for an indefinite period?”
Framed that way, of course some people hesitate to say yes.
But formal mentorship isn’t the only way to benefit from the wisdom of those who came before. I’ve never formally asked anyone to mentor me. And yet I’ve had dozens of unofficial mentors.
The Copy-Paste Method
One way to learn from others is by copying what you observe. 
Sometimes this means reading books or blogs from engineers you respect and directly applying their ideas to your work.
I’ve also been fortunate to work alongside some extremely talented engineers, and I shamelessly copied the things they did well.
When I meet one of these engineers, I try to figure out what they’re doing differently: How do they approach a problem? What do they read? How do they communicate in meetings? What do they know that I don’t?
Then I steal whatever seems useful and apply it to my own career.
Great artists steal. Engineers should too.
Curiosity Compounds
Still, just observing has its limits. Asking questions can get you even farther. 
I’ve asked managers how they approached difficult conversations, and I’ve asked engineers what their process was for solving problems I thought were impossible.

author: Allison Marsh
title: The First Battery Was Inspired By a Dead Frog
content:
In a display case on the lower level of the Faraday Museum at the Royal Institution in London, there’s an unassuming stack of gray metal discs and blotting paper. It’s not at all obvious that this humble object is the starting point of today’s multibillion-dollar global battery industry. The object’s invention in 1799 grew out of a disagreement that Alessandro Volta—the Italian physicist for whom the unit of measurement for electrical potential is named—had with his friend Luigi Galvani over a dead frog.

The Debate Over Animal Electricity 
Galvani was a well-respected Italian physician. In the 1770s, he began investigating the use of electricity to stimulate the muscles of dissected frogs. Armed with an electrostatic generator and an early type of capacitor called a Leyden jar, he was able to create a charge, store it, and then zap his animal specimens at will. He was intrigued when the frog legs twitched as if they were still alive. He spent the last three decades of the 18th century studying the phenomenon, and in 1791, he published De viribus electricitatis in motu musculari commentarius (Commentary on the Effect of Electricity on Muscular Motion).
  Luigi Galvani spent decades investigating what he believed to be a natural electric force emanating from animals. Universal History Archive/Getty Images
Galvani saw the frog as embodying an “animal electricity,” an innate vital force that activated nerves and muscles, similar to what had been observed in (living) electric eels and torpedo rays. For Galvani, the frog was an electrical machine analogous to a Leyden jar. The brain was the source of the electrical charge; the nerves conducted the electrical fluid; and the muscles stored opposite charges. The illustrations in his 1791 book are fabulous—frog legs spread all over his laboratory table!

title: The E.U.’s AI Drive Undermines Its ​Own Chip Strategy
content:
This story was originally published by Tech Policy Press.
The European Union’s push for technological sovereignty faces an uncomfortable contradiction.
As the E.U. rolls out AI factories, gigafactories, and new data centers, it is creating a surge in demand for the advanced semiconductors that underpin artificial intelligence. Yet Europe produces fewer than 10 percent of the world’s chips and remains heavily dependent on U.S. designers and Asian manufacturers for the most advanced processors.
That tension sits at the heart of Chips Act 2.0, the European Commission’s planned overhaul of its flagship semiconductor strategy.
The original Chips Act, adopted in 2023, sought to raise Europe’s share of global semiconductor production to 20 percent by 2030. But the European Court of Auditors has warned that target is unlikely to be met, while the Commission’s own projections put Europe’s market share at about 11.7 percent.
The Commission now wants to correct what officials see as a major weakness in the first law: It focused on expanding supply without doing enough to stimulate demand. To address that gap, Chips Act 2.0 is expected to introduce demand-side measures, including public procurement tools, demand accelerators, and closer coordination between semiconductor producers and industrial users. The Commission’s calculation is straightforward: Stronger domestic demand will encourage companies to invest in designing and manufacturing chips in Europe.
But the strategy carries a paradox. The AI infrastructure that the Commission hopes will anchor a European semiconductor ecosystem will initially rely almost entirely on advanced processors designed by U.S. companies and manufactured in Asia.
“Key positions are held by a small number of firms, mostly outside Europe,” Claire Godfrey, executive director of the Balanced Economy Project, told Tech Policy Press.

author: Harry Goldstein
title: Noodling on Nuclear Engines
content:
One day in 1982, Joseph “Rod” Canion and two colleagues from Texas Instruments sat down at the House of Pies in Houston and used a placemat to sketch out what would become Compaq’s portable PC. In 1996, Felix Zandman, founder of Vishay Intertechnology, dined at Husker Steak House in Columbus, Neb., grabbed a napkin and drafted a design for a power metal strip resistor, which became crucial to power-management components in industrial, automotive, and consumer applications. Now that wispy piece of paper resides at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History. Perhaps most famously, Robert Metcalfe, working at Xerox PARC in 1973, roughed out some early designs for what would become Ethernet, though contrary to popular belief, no napkin was involved.
Yet another napkin (see above) was pressed into service last year, when Kurt Polzin, chief engineer of the space nuclear propulsion project at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center, met Robert ­Schleicher of General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems at a conference and started talking about nuclear rocket design.
“They did the classic let’s-sketch-out-an-idea-on-a-napkin,” says IEEE Spectrum’s Special Projects Editor and our in-house spaceflight expert Stephen Cass. “This rocket engine is still at the paper-planning stage, which, to be fair, is where most of NASA’s humans-to-Mars planning has been for the last 60 years.”
